"Create a massive, flat 3D survival game map featuring a realistic and high-depth PBR texture pack. To prevent lag and ensure high FPS, divide the entire world into a chunk-based streaming system that dynamically loads nearby chunks and unloads distant ones. Additionally, optimize performance by implementing Level of Detail (LOD) for distant objects, Frustum Culling to render only what is on screen, Occlusion Culling to hide objects behind walls or terrain, and GPU Instancing for repeated elements like trees, rocks, and grass. Keep the lighting baked where possible and optimize shadow draw distances.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable flat 3D wilderness survival game with a polished HUD, chunk streaming, PBR-style materials, and performance-oriented rendering.

## Requirements
- Include chunk-based world streaming that loads nearby chunks and unloads distant chunks.
- Implement frustum culling, LOD-friendly distant rendering, occlusion-aware design, GPU instancing, baked-style lighting, and limited shadow distances.
- Provide realistic survival gameplay and high FPS optimization.
- Add mobile-responsive controls and usable desktop controls.

## Decisions
- Used Three.js as the single-page WebGL implementation.
- Assumed a browser-based game with keyboard/mouse controls and no external assets.
- Used procedural canvas textures and instanced meshes to avoid asset-download overhead.
- Used 80-unit chunks with a 2-chunk view radius.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the complete single-page game interface and HUD in `index.html`.
- Added procedural PBR-style terrain, normal/detail textures, trees, rocks, bushes, grass, flowers, and campfires.
- Added chunk streaming, InstancedMesh rendering, terrain height variation, fog, shadow limits, frustum culling, survival stats, gathering, crafting, inventory, map, day/night cycle, and death/restart flow.
- Started a local HTTP server on port 3002.
- Installed the Playwright Chromium browser for visual verification.
- Captured a viewport JPEG with the Playwright CLI.

### Active
- None.

### Blocked

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a playable browser-based 3D wilderness survival game and enhance it with a third-person character, mobile controls, and better mobile performance.
- Current request: optimize physics calculations for mobile devices.

## Requirements
- Chunk-streamed wilderness, survival gameplay, polished HUD, and performance-focused rendering.
- Third-person camera that smoothly follows the player from an elevated angle.
- Responsive mobile joystick and action buttons for jump, interact, and attack.
- Articulated humanoid character with joint/limb animation, surface-adaptive feet, and physical interaction with world items.
- Optimize physics calculations for mobile devices.

## Decisions
- Use a single-page Three.js implementation in `index.html` with procedural assets and no external models or physics library.
- Use lightweight custom movement/jump logic rather than a full rigid-body physics engine.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented survival game, chunk streaming, procedural world, HUD, gathering, crafting, and survival systems in `index.html`.
- Added third-person follow camera, procedural humanoid rig and limb animation, jumping, attack animation, mobile joystick, and mobile action buttons.
- Verified mobile viewport controls are visible and browser reports no errors.

### Active
- Optimize physics/frame-loop calculations for mobile; initial inspection identified per-frame allocations and repeated work, but no optimization changes have yet been applied.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Optimize `step()` and `animate()` in `index.html`: reduce per-frame allocations, avoid unnecessary updates, and lower-frequency mobile-only work where appropriate.
2. Test the optimized game in mobile and desktop browser viewports and check for runtime errors.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Main single-page game; camera, character, controls, and frame/physics loops are implemented here.

## Important Context
- Local server is available at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Latest inspected hotspots: `step()` allocates temporary `THREE.Vector3`s each frame and calls `updateHUD()`/`setTime()` each frame; `animate()` updates character and fire effects every frame.
- The latest mobile smoke test showed joystick and jump controls visible with no console errors.
